frame: Wren is studying platypuses. The Bridgle is carrying facts between her book and her notes.
text: Text A (an encyclopedia entry): The platypus is a small, shy animal found in rivers and creeks in eastern Australia. It has a flat bill like a duck's, webbed feet and thick brown fur. Platypuses dive underwater to hunt for food, with their eyes, ears and nostrils shut. Instead, they find food by sensing tiny electric signals from the bodies of worms, shrimp and insect larvae. Males have a sharp spur on each back leg that can deliver a painful venom. Text B (Wren's survey notes): Spent the whole evening at Stringybark Creek. Saw two platypuses just after sunset, diving again and again near the fallen log to find food. Each dive lasted about thirty seconds. One came up chewing so hard that I could hear it. Gravel in its cheeks helps it grind up food, because adults have no teeth. Counted fifty-six dives in an hour. Did not see the sharp spurs that males have on their back legs, so they may both have been females.

frame: Zed is arguing with Narra the Teller about who the hero of this story is. The Pointern is the referee.
text: Commander Ray had flown the starship Dusty for twenty years, and he never let anyone forget it. His crew had heard his stories so many times that they could say them along with him. When a meteor storm hit, he shouted orders from his big gold chair. Most of them were wrong. 'Turn left!' he yelled, and the ship flew straight into a rock. While the commander shouted, Pip, the ship's little cleaning robot, rolled quietly into the engine room. Pip was so small that most of the crew forgot it was there. Pip found the cracked fuel line and wrapped it in tape. Then it worked out a safe path through the storm, one rock at a time, and whispered the directions to the pilot. The Dusty made it through without another scratch. Back on Earth, Commander Ray made a long speech about leadership and didn't mention Pip once. Pip was in the corner, cleaning up the cake crumbs from the party.
